text:
ash_oncall: incident-bot paged on ap-south1: spike in gateway timeouts and 504s starting ~02:14 UTC. several customers reporting partial failures. paging rule: gateway-504-rate > 4% for 5m :rotating_light:

incident-bot: [ALERT] ap-south1 - gateway 504/timeouts elevated. link: https://pager.redwood.internal/incident/2146004321

nina_sre: i'm seeing long accept queues on gateway-proxy instances and many connections in CLOSE_WAIT. p95 latency flat but p99 skyrocketed.

raj_infra: any recent infra changes in ap-south1? load balancer or node pool scaling?

tomasz: we had a scheduled autoscaler policy test at 01:50 UTC that increased max pods but that shouldn't affect connection state. no config flips after that.

claire_support: customers are seeing requests hang ~12s then 504. A few session-heavy customers (chat widgets) impacted. collecting customer IDs.

ash_oncall: priority: 1) reduce user-visible errors, 2) find whether it's network, gateway, or backend saturation. start failover plan to ap-south1-secondary (ap-south1-b) and ap-east1 for non-sticky sessions.

nina_sre: trying to lift circuit-breaker thresholds on gateway-proxy to allow more inflight connections. current cb settings tripping at 200 errors/10s.

tomasz: cb tweak command:
```
redwoodctl proxy set-cb --service gateway-proxy --region ap-south1 --threshold 500 --window 30s
```

ops-bot: command executed: set-cb request_id=cb-2146-01. note: changing CB may increase backend load.

nina_sre: after increasing threshold, error rate dipped slightly but tail remains. traces show long TCP handshake/slow start issues between edge LB and gateway instances.

raj_infra: looking at LB metrics: backend health shows some instances reporting high socket backlog and kernel-level SYN_RECV. Might be ephemeral port exhaustion on nodes.

ash_oncall: can we add more NAT IPs / ephemeral ports? Also start redirecting new sessions away from problematic nodes.

tomasz: adding ephemeral ports via infra flag now. command:
```
infractl node update-ephemeral-ports --pool ap-south1-gw --add 20000
```

ops-bot: node update submitted: request_id=np-2146-67. changes will roll over as nodes restart.

claire_support: meanwhile customers ask for ETA. advise them we are routing new traffic to alternate region for reduced latency impact.

nina_sre: enabling stateless routing fallback so sessions won't be stuck to old connections. toggling sticky-sessions=false for LB in ap-south1.

```
redwoodctl lb config set --region ap-south1 --sticky-sessions false --force
```

ops-bot: LB config change applied. note: existing sticky sessions may still hit old backends until cookie TTL expires.

ash_oncall: start draining gateway-proxy pods with high accept_queue values to force clients to reconnect (they'll land on healthy pods or fallback region). use graceful drain 45s.

tomasz: drain command:
```
kubectl cordon gw-node-22 && kubectl drain gw-node-22 --grace-period=45 --ignore-daemonsets
```

ops-bot: drain orchestration started: drain_id=dr-2146-12. multiple nodes scheduled for rolling drain.

nina_sre: after draining two nodes, 504 rate declined from 5.1% -> 1.4% within 90s. connection metrics show fewer CLOSE_WAIT sockets.

raj_infra: there are also a handful of gateway pods showing repeated JVM GC pauses (old model of gateway uses JVM). suspect memory pressure leading to long pauses and accept queue buildup. logs:
```
[02:16:03] WARN GC pause 1276ms heap=3.8G/6G
[02:17:18] ERROR accept timeout server socket backlog=1024
```

ash_oncall: schedule rolling restart for gateway pods with high GC time and patch limit on heap size to reduce pause. Also bump pod replicas temporarily.

tomasz: scaling replicas:
```
kubectl scale deployment/gateway-proxy --replicas=12 -n infra-ap-south1
```

ops-bot: scale request accepted: scale_id=sc-2146-90. new pods provisioning.

claire_support: support notified customers about failover to ap-east1 and temporary retry guidance.

nina_sre: monitoring: p99 latency dropping, accept queues steady. we've recovered most user traffic. still checking for any downstream backend errors that would persist after reconnections.

raj_infra: follow-up: investigate why ephemeral port exhaustion happened — possible leak in outbound connections from gateway to backends or NAT gateway throttling. creating infra ticket INFRA-2146.

ash_oncall: handoff plan: SRE owns post-incident monitoring for 4 hours, infra to investigate port usage and NAT config, eng-runtime to look at JVM tuning and socket handling. create postmortem with timeline, customer impact, mitigation commands used, and detection gaps.

incident-bot: incident annotated: "ap-south1 gateway accept-queue and socket exhaustion -> increased 504s; mitigations: CB relax, ephemeral ports increase, disable stickiness, drain + restart pods, scale replicas; fallback routing for new sessions." severity: Sev-2.

claire_support: initial customer impact window: 02:14 - 02:23 UTC. affected customers: CUST-3101, CUST-7782, CUST-9982 (chat widgets) — compiling full list for credits.

nina_sre: action items: 1) add alert for kernel SYN_RECV/backlog > 800, 2) add NAT ephemeral port consumption monitor, 3) run chaos test for sticky session fallback, 4) JVM GC tuning RFC.

ash_oncall: thanks team. we'll review in a blameless postmortem tomorrow. leaving notes: commands run (set-cb, lb config, node update-ephemeral-ports, drains, scale), ops request ids (cb-2146-01, np-2146-67, sc-2146-90, dr-2146-12). :thumbsup:
